exposure: moderate/severe urinary incontinence symptoms during pregnancy
self-reported family history of pelvic organ prolapse or urinary incontinence (FHPOP/UI+)
outcome: self-reported family history of pelvic organ prolapse or urinary incontinence (FHPOP/UI+)
anatomic pelvic organ prolapse (POP) at 1-year postpartum
cohort: The study participants were nulliparous women who were followed from the third trimester of their first pregnancy through 1-year postpartum.
finding: The study found that self-reported family history of pelvic organ prolapse or urinary incontinence (FHPOP/UI+) was associated with various demographic and clinical factors, and FHPOP/UI+ itself was associated with moderate/severe urinary incontinence but not anatomic pelvic organ prolapse at 1-year postpartum.
mod_finding: The odds of reporting a positive family history of pelvic organ prolapse or urinary incontinence decreased if the participant's mother delivered via cesarean.
